Zelensky:
During this year of war, we have received dozens, perhaps a few hundred, missiles to defend our skies.
Middle Eastern countries used about 2,000 in the first 48 hours of the war.
That doesn't mean we shouldn't support Middle Eastern allies. Of course we should support them, help them and defend them.
But everything has to be competitive.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Zelensky:
We told our American partners: Switch on Starlink in those parts of Russia where they launch ballistic missiles.
Why must we all be under attack? Why must all of Europe be afraid that Russian ballistic missiles will reach European territory?
Switch on Starlink. We will do it. We will handle it.
Of course, we will do it if Russia doesn't stop this war.
Switch it on. It's not difficult, really.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Zelensky:
Russia produces 140 ballistic missiles every month, and they already have 700 ballistic missiles in storage.
Everybody talks about these missiles, but you can solve this problem.
About 70% of the components in each ballistic missile come from other countries — Asia, the United States and Europe.
You can stop it because these are your companies. Worldwide companies are selling these components to Russia.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Zelensky:
Some countries think they need to keep their interceptors for themselves. They are ready to help Ukraine, but first they need to defend themselves.
But that will not help if Ukraine falls, if Russia breaks our defensive lines.
Nobody can defend themselves alone against a country that is ready to do anything, that is ready to kill ordinary civilians with missiles and drones.
They already have an army of around 2 million. There is no European country with an army that strong. European armies are not ready for such a struggle.

events.text:
⚡🇷🇺🇮🇷 As the region is on the brink of an inevitable explosion, Iran unveils its own drone production line, while Russia introduces new modifications to its Shahed 136 (Geran) drones.
Recently, Russia has introduced jet-powered drones equipped with what appear to be "mustaches" which have demonstrated significant effectiveness in strikes targeting bridges, pipelines, and power transmission towers.
These "mustaches" are contact sensors, and the drones carry an explosive payload capable of cutting through metals instead of causing a large scale explosion. Their speed has tripled, and they have become much harder to intercept.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: New footage from Oryol shows Ukrainian Storm Shadow / SCALP-EG missiles hit the Proton Plant. At least 13 people are now reported dead at the Proton plant, including 11 women. Many more are reportedly trapped under the rubble, while ongoing fires are still preventing emergency crews from reaching them.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Another video from the Ukrainian Storm Shadow cruise missile attack in Oryol appeared.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: ❗️Zelensky says Starlink and Starshield speed restrictions are still in place and that interceptor deliveries needed to protect Ukraine from Russian ballistic missiles remain delayed. “This is a real problem, because the Russians attack us almost every day,” he said. Zelensky added that Ukraine wants strong, genuinely friendly relations with the US and other partners, without misunderstandings.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: As we reported earlier... Russian sources are now increasingly reporting significant personnel losses from the strike on the Proton plant in Oryol, including valuable engineers and specialized staff. One Russian report also says people remain trapped in the basement. Proton produces optoelectronics and electronic components used in Kh-101 cruise missiles, Iskander-M ballistic missiles and Pantsir-S1 air-defense systems.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: ❗️ Local channels report mass sightings of Ukrainian drones moving toward Moscow region through Oryol and Tula regions.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: A crashed drone was found about 100 meters from a home in Chiștelnița, Telenești district in Moldova. Police say no casualties have been reported. Officers cordoned off the area, while explosives specialists are heading to the scene to examine the drone and determine the circumstances.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Additional footage of 2 Storm Shadow / SCALP-EG cruise missiles striking Oryol. We are leaning towards 4/4 instead of 3/4 hits on the Proton Plant, based on the footage.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Detailed impact footage from Oryol confirms 3-4 hits on the Proton plant. The facility produces optoelectronic and semiconductor components and is linked to Russia's defense-industrial supply chain, including components used in missile and air-defense systems.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: Aftermath footage from Oryol shows significant destruction following the Ukrainian missile attack. The damaged site is identified as the Proton plant, a semiconductor manufacturer in the city.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: A group of four cruise missiles (likely SCALP-EG/Storm Shadow) launched from the Sumy region headed toward Kursk, took a strong turn to the north and struck Oryol. At least three impacts were recorded, a fourth is yet to be determined, but possibly one was shot down.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: ❗️❗️Ukrainian missiles struck Oryol this afternoon. Locals say the Proton plant, a semiconductor manufacturer, may have been targeted. Footage shows multiple impacts landing close together, but the extent of damage is not yet clear.

events.text:
🇮🇷Tehran prepares to strike undersea cables if US-Israeli attacks resume - report
The attacks would be aimed at underwater communications cable in the Persian Gulf region, Reuters claims, citing two unnamed Iranian security officials.
"If Iran is attacked, there will be no more red lines... from undersea cables to military bases, including covert ones," one of the officials said as quoted by the media agency.
The officials pointed out that Iran has full access to the cables and warned the US not to “play with fire.”
Earlier this week, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps pointedly [warned](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/76498) that “seven major internet cables run beneath the Strait of Hormuz.”
Iranian Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei also warned that Iran could target undersea internet cables, data centers, and AI facilities linked to the US if hostilities are resumed.
